brief.overview: 本期覆盖 2026-10-18 13:00 至 10-19 13:00（UTC）。OpenAI、Hugging Face、Google 三个来源近 24 小时无条目；TechCrunch 仅两条公司或人事动态，按排除偏好未收录。可用的相关技术信息来自 arXiv cs.AI/cs.LG 当日公告的论文，按其与「Agent／工具调用／AI 编程／本地部署」的贴合度收录 5 篇。需说明：这 5 篇的首次提交日期多为 2026-10-15（SAI 为 2026-07-27），10-19 只是进入 arXiv 新公告流的时间，并非当天首次发表；以上均为论文自评结果，未经独立复现。

items.title: Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides
items.summary: 论文提出 Structured Authority Injection（SAI）：把运维人员的修正改写为带类型、经 schema 校验的 MCP 工具调用注入 agent，并在每次 LLM 提示前附加一个带优先级的“授权上下文”，无需微调。摘要给出三类覆盖（约束/优先级/策略）与显式优先级排序，并称修正通过规划进程无法访问的专用通道生效。作者在 9 个 LLM、8 个面向 agent 失效模式的场景上评测，报告减少了指令歧义解读、缓解了多轮规划中的“授权衰减”；提示开销在最强模型上最多降低 38%（论文注明具体取决于模型与场景，收益差异很大）。该论文 7 月 27 日首次提交，10 月 19 日进入公告流，不是新近首发。
items.why_it_matters: 你做后端与工具调用，SAI 的思路可直接映射到内部 agent 平台的“运行时权限层”：把人的修正做成可审计、可校验的 MCP 调用，而不是改 prompt 或改代码。注意两点：38% 只是部分模型上的提示开销降幅，不是普遍结论；把外部输入变成工具调用通道也意味着要自己补鉴权与注入防护。

items.title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards
items.summary: Lean4AgenticRL 将多级过程奖励（低层工具调用奖励与中层工作流阶段奖励）统一到 Lean4 形式化框架中，用于开放式 agent RL，并配合 workflow-stage-normalized GRPO 训练，同时构建了问题专属的 workflow 系统以支持验证。作者报告 LAR-27B 在 TerminalBench-2.1 上达到 77.3%；模型平均比基座模型高 9.89%、比其所知的同规模第二好模型高 5.07%（原文只给百分比数字，未说明是相对提升还是百分点）。论文 10 月 15 日首次提交，10 月 19 日进入公告流；未提到权重或训练代码是否开源。
items.why_it_matters: 如果你在做代码/终端类 agent 的后训练，这套“工具调用级 + 阶段级”双层奖励比只在最终结果上给奖励更可操作，也便于定位失败环节。落地前需确认开源情况；9.89%/5.07% 的表述口径不清，不要直接当成百分点写进内部结论。

items.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
items.summary: 论文将 harness 演进带来的分数增益拆为三部分：伪影过拟合、测试期扩展、残差（可泛化的上界），据此提出 Harness-Delta Attribution。在 11 个执行模型、3 个 harness 演进框架，以及数学/代码/创意/agent 任务设置上，筛出 21 个在搜索集上有统计显著增益的设置：过拟合平均解释 54% 的增益，测试期扩展解释 14%，二者合计在 14 个设置中超过 50%。作者还报告搜索集增益常无法迁移到留出任务，基于验证集的选择不足以防止过拟合。论文 10 月 15 日首次提交，10 月 19 日公告。
items.why_it_matters: 你在后端优化 agent 工具链、提示或验证环时，这类归因能回答“涨点是不是真的”：先固定 held-out 集，同时记录 token 与采样次数，否则很容易把多花算力和评测集记忆当成 harness 改进。54%/14% 是这 21 个设置上的平均值，不适用于所有基准。

items.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
items.summary: PRIME 针对多步工具调用中的「结论是否被证据支撑」：它在检查前先固定每条结论可被正当化的证据路径（evidence routes），并由独立程序记录每次检查结果、拒绝结果无法支撑的结论，同时提示 agent 去做能支撑更强结论的检查或代为执行。在 480 个公共记录任务上，直接向 agent 出示需求说明时，有 26.7% 的任务给出了无依据结论，而 PRIME 为 0 例；其方向与附加检查把「有依据结论」的平均分从仅拒绝作答时的 30.1 提高到最高实测 59.2（满分 100）。论文 10 月 15 日首次提交，10 月 19 日进入公告流。
items.why_it_matters: 你如果做数据核查、报表或对账类 agent，PRIME 的问题设定和你日常场景很接近：模型往往“答得像”而非“查得到”。可借鉴的是把每条结论绑定到具体记录与规则检查，而不只是加“请核实”的提示；注意这是作者自建的合成流水线，真实业务分布会更脏。

items.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
items.summary: SPOT 给扩散语言模型做推测解码：一个仅 0.62M 参数的小模型只读目标模型的输出分布，预测“先填哪个位置”的提交顺序并生成候选树，目标模型一次前向并行验证全部候选；作者另提出 coupled-noise match verification，使该方法在任意采样温度下仍成立。实验报告目标模型前向次数最多减少 6.8 倍、吞吐最多达到标准解码的 3.2 倍，在 T=0 与 T=1 的各任务和预算下均优于校准型与免训练草稿基线；同一个草稿器可跨 6 个扩散语言模型迁移。论文 10 月 15 日首次提交，10 月 19 日公告。
items.why_it_matters: 与“本地部署”直接相关：草稿器只有 0.62M 参数、可跨模型复用，意味着加速成本主要在工程集成而非额外显存。但测的是扩散语言模型而非目前主流的自回归模型，且 6.8×/3.2× 是论文实验配置下的最好结果；若你本地跑的是 llama.cpp/vLLM 之类的自回归栈，暂时只能作为技术观察。

{"id": "da92b80397690dde35e8", "title": "Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22373", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-07-27T03:38:01+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-07-27T03:38:01+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous orchestrators in distributed and multi-agent systems, yet a control gap remains: no protocol-level mechanism allows human operators to inject binding directives that persist across planning cycles. {"id": "a97c1f5a709e4de6f7ba", "title": "Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22448", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T15:26:54+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T15:26:54+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective. To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL. **Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system. It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm. Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size. **LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1. {"id": "f34ad45741b405ff9e69", "title": "Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T17:39:38+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T17:39:38+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? {"id": "051009ada2a4f647f6fc", "title": "On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22543", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T18:40:42+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T18:40:42+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) promise parallel text generation, but in practice face an unresolved speed-quality trade-off. Exact decoding fills in only one masked position per model pass, while faster multi-token decoding schemes are lossy. Speculative decoding is the standard lossless acceleration for autoregressive models. However, it does not transfer directly to DLMs, which must choose both what to generate and where. We show that this order is the missing piece: the model's own predictions from the previous pass already give the right token at 92-100% of positions, but not which position comes next. A 0.62M-parameter model reads only the target's output distributions and proposes a tree of candidate continuations, and the target verifies all of them in a single pass by checking whether each equals its own next state. On the verification side, our analysis shows that prior block-diffusion verification approaches either assume $T=0$ or a sequential proposal interface. To support tree-based speculation at any temperature, we propose using coupled-noise match verification for diffusion blocks, following shared-Gumbel-noise coupling approaches. Our comprehensive experiments show that SPOT cuts target passes by up to 6.8x and reaches up to 3.2x the throughput of standard decoding, beating the calibrated and training-free drafting baselines in every task and budget at $T=0$ and $T=1$. selected_evidence.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) promise parallel text generation, but in practice face an unresolved speed-quality trade-off. Exact decoding fills in only one masked position per model pass, while faster multi-token decoding schemes are lossy. Speculative decoding is the standard lossless acceleration for autoregressive models. However, it does not transfer directly to DLMs, which must choose both what to generate and where. We show that this order is the missing piece: the model's own predictions from the previous pass already give the right token at 92-100% of positions, but not which position comes next. Based on this observation, we introduce Speculating Positions Order Trajectory (SPOT), which learns to predict this order. A 0.62M-parameter model reads only the target's output distributions and proposes a tree of candidate continuations, and the target verifies all of them in a single pass by checking whether each equals its own next state. On the verification side, our analysis shows that prior block-diffusion verification approaches either assume $T=0$ or a sequential proposal interface. To support tree-based speculation at any temperature, we propose using coupled-noise match verification for diffusion blocks, following shared-Gumbel-noise coupling approaches. Our comprehensive experiments show that SPOT cuts target passes by up to 6.8x and reaches up to 3.2x the throughput of standard decoding, beating the calibrated and training-free drafting baselines in every task and budget at $T=0$ and $T=1$. In addition, we show that the learned drafter transfers across models, demonstrating successful transfer across six different DLMs. Project page: this https URL

selected_evidence.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link. Agents fail by accepting a report after a required check has failed, or by settling for a weaker conclusion without trying another way that could still succeed. We introduce PRIME (Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence). Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself. PRIME reports only conclusions authorized by its rules and ledger. With correct requirements, exact checks at known locations, and sufficient budget at stopping, completion reaches the strongest supported conclusion. On 480 public-record tasks, an agent shown the requirements reported unjustified conclusions on 26.7% of tasks, while PRIME reported none. Its directions and added checks raised the average score for justified conclusions from 30.1, with refusal alone, to the maximum of 59.2 out of 100.

selected_evidence.title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective. To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL. **Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system. It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm. Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size. **LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1. On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**. These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open-ended agentic RL.

selected_evidence.title: Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous orchestrators in distributed and multi-agent systems, yet a control gap remains: no protocol-level mechanism allows human operators to inject binding directives that persist across planning cycles. Free-text overrides suffer from ambiguous interpretation due to lack of schema validation and from authority erosion as operator instructions lose influence within accumulating context. We propose Structured Authority Injection (SAI), a protocol that addresses these issues by routing operator corrections through typed, schema-validated Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and maintaining a ranked authority context prepended to each LLM prompt. SAI defines three override classes (Constraint, Priority, and Strategy) with distinct persistence semantics and an explicit precedence order enforced via a directed authority channel inaccessible to the planning process. The method requires no model fine-tuning or access to model weights and applies to instruction-tuned LLMs supporting MCP tool use. Evaluation across nine LLMs and eight scenarios targeting agent failure modes shows reduced ambiguous directive interpretation and mitigated authority decay across planning iterations, with lower prompt overhead in the strongest models (up to 38% depending on model and scenario), though benefit varies substantially across models. SAI provides a general design pattern for agent systems requiring explicit and persistent human control.

selected_evidence.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research.

evidence_quotes: we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement.

We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling.
among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings.

items.corrected_summary: PRIME 针对多步工具调用中的「结论是否被证据支撑」：它在检查前先固定每条结论可被正当化的证据路径（evidence routes），并由独立程序记录每次检查结果、拒绝结果无法支撑的结论，同时提示 agent 去做能支撑更强结论的检查或代为执行。在 480 个公共记录任务上，直接向 agent 出示需求说明时，有 26.7% 的任务给出了无依据结论，而 PRIME 为 0 例；其方向与附加检查把「有依据结论」的平均分从仅拒绝作答时的 30.1 提高到最高实测 59.2（满分 100）。论文 10 月 15 日首次提交，10 月 19 日进入公告流。

evidence_quotes: Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself.

On 480 public-record tasks, an agent shown the requirements reported unjustified conclusions on 26.7% of tasks, while PRIME reported none. Its directions and added checks raised the average score for justified conclusions from 30.1, with refusal alone, to the maximum of 59.2 out of 100.

evidence_quotes: A 0.62M-parameter model reads only the target's output distributions and proposes a tree of candidate continuations, and the target verifies all of them in a single pass by checking whether each equals its own next state.
To support tree-based speculation at any temperature, we propose using coupled-noise match verification for diffusion blocks, following shared-Gumbel-noise coupling approaches.

Our comprehensive experiments show that SPOT cuts target passes by up to 6.8x and reaches up to 3.2x the throughput of standard decoding, beating the calibrated and training-free drafting baselines in every task and budget at $T=0$ and $T=1$.
